input.quote: 11.5 Special, Indirect, and Other Losses. EXCEPT (A) FOR FRAUD, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE, (B) FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS UNDER [ARTICLE 9 OR SECTION 5.8], (C) AS PROVIDED UNDER [***] AND (D) TO THE EXTENT ANY SUCH DAMAGES ARE REQUIRED TO BE PAID TO A THIRD PARTY AS PART OF A CLAIM FOR WHICH A PARTY PROVIDES INDEMNIFICATION UNDER THIS ARTICLE 11, NEITHER PARTY NOR ANY OF ITS AFFILIATES SHALL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES
input.rationale:
There is no aggregate monetary liability cap anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for "aggregate liability", "shall not exceed", "limitation of liability", "maximum liability", "sole remedy" and "damages" return only: (i) Section 11.5 (p0572), a mutual, all-caps exclusion of indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive and consequential damages, carved out mutually for fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, breach of Article 9 (Confidentiality) or Section 5.8, and third-party damages payable under an Article 11 indemnity; (ii) the mutual indemnities in Sections 11.1/11.2 (p0559-p0560); and (iii) insurance minimums in Section 11.6. The only "maximum aggregate" figures are payment ceilings in Article 6 (milestones), not liability caps.

Consequently the fallback cap elements are not literally met — there is no mutual cap and no 12-months-of-fees basis — while the four carve-out elements (indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct) are satisfied on the face of Section 11.5 and, in any event, trivially so because no cap constrains them. Crucially, the regime is fully symmetric: neither Harpoon's nor AbbVie's direct liability is limited, so none of the walk-away triggers (our liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; a sub-6-month Vendor cap; indemnities inside a cap) is present.

I have not proposed a redline. Introducing the preferred or fallback cap would, for the first time, cap Harpoon's direct exposure to us and cut off our recovery under the Section 11.2 indemnity and Article 10 warranties. It also has no workable basis here: this Development and Option Agreement has no recurring "fees" — consideration is an upfront/option payment, milestones under Sections 6.2-6.3 and royalties on Net Sales — so a "12 months' fees" measure is either illusory or arbitrary. The trade-off (limiting our own uncapped exposure under the Section 11.1 indemnity versus preserving unlimited recourse against Harpoon) is a commercial call for the deal team; if the business wants an outer limit, we should seek a mutual cap expressed as a percentage of amounts paid or payable by AbbVie, with Section 11.5's existing carve-outs (plus IP infringement and AbbVie's payment obligations) sitting outside it, rather than a fee-multiple formula.
